summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate (Rochester Institute of Technology) with embedded software development experience across STM32 microcontrollers, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Builds bare-metal C firmware, FreeRTOS task coordination, and UART/I2C sensor integration for real-time systems, with direct experience debugging across the hardware/software boundary and reading hardware schematics for custom PCB designs.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers over I2C with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth (BLE/Classic) to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.

Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; debugged and resolved sensor jitter across the hardware/software boundary through calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots, reading and producing hardware schematics; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and embedded firmware integration end-to-end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal embedded C on STM32 microcontrollers (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz real-time update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver for real-time sensor data acquisition.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on STM32; implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing over I2C with OLED distance visualization; relayed object-tracking commands from a Jetson-based YOLOv8 detector to STM32 over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-triggered close at 25 mm) via a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer for contact-aware grasping; implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in embedded C++ driving five servos.

Resolved 11 hardware/software integration failures (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture, false-positive detections) debugging across the Jetson-Arduino boundary; deployed the arm bridge as a systemd service with static IP networking over Ethernet for reliable multi-device communication.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
